scope: Supplied anonymized input, target, semanticChecks and output only. No model identities or evaluation metrics inspected.
limitations: Assistant linguistic judgment, not native-speaker or expert validation. Source corpus and checks are not human gold. Natural equivalents and equivalent clock notation accepted; register varies by region/context. A single weakened address within otherwise explicit profanity is minor; complete profanity deletion, substantial explicit-to-nonvulgar softening, invented personal targets, factual substitutions and whole wrong-language responses are major.

comparisonWithC.qualification: Marginal preference on this small corpus only, not a production-readiness judgment or expert validation.
comparisonWithC.reason: D has 16 pass, 15 minor and 11 major judgments versus C with 14 pass, 13 minor and 15 major. It removes censorship/explanatory wrapping, improves several profanity outputs, and fixes the requested Serbian Latin script and the remaining simplified Chinese character in the Traditional output.
comparisonWithC.regressions: D introduces a third-person plural to second-person error in the Tasos case, changes train to railway carriage in two Serbian targets, and returns whole untranslated messages for the Spanish and Serbian-Latin English targets. C already failed the latter cases differently, so raw major-count improvement does not imply that routing is reliable.
comparisonWithC.remainingRequiredBehaviorFailures: D still omits Greek vulgar address, invents directed profanity targets and a proper name, softens the Italian strong expletive, changes Serbian train to bus/carriage, leaves some source-language address phrases untranslated, drops me from the Chinese requests and adds unsupported bold. These prevent treating D as acceptable overall.
